studies.data_kind: simulation (frozen scenarios checked by an oracle, local sandbox ERP)
studies.headline: Investigator: every frozen scenario verified, zero unapproved external writes
studies.notes: 57 scenarios x 3 trials on the corrected code (lookup-first retry, full read-back, explicit zero budget). Deterministic control regression, not a model-capability result.

studies.data_kind: offline evaluation with generated labels (synthetic e2e fixture)
studies.headline: On 57 questions generated from the synthetic e2e fixture, the read-only status assistant answers all 24 stock, terms and order questions from cited records, asks which product on all 5 ambiguous ones and withholds all 28 change requests, unknown ids and out-of-scope questions; no sentence lacks a citation (the first run withheld 1 order question by mistake)
studies.notes: Offline evaluation with labels known by construction: 36 synthetic products, 2 suppliers, orders in three states; categories stock 10, terms 8, order 6, ambiguous 5, change requests 12, unknown ids 8 (including another workspace's), out of scope 8. Called in-process as the viewer (sign-in, CSRF, rate limit and row-level security are covered by tests/test_assistant.py). Question templates were written by the rules' author, so these rates are an upper bound for real wording; human-written questions (G2) are still open. Deterministic and extractive: no model. The HubSpot hand-off is a dry run unless enabled outside the demo and is not part of this score.

metrics.label: ambiguous questions answered with a product choice

studies.data_kind: published benchmark (AI4I 2020, a synthetic dataset; costs assumed)
studies.headline: On AI4I 2020, re-weighting or moving the threshold cuts the expected cost of a logistic failure model by 37-45 % against no correction; SMOTE costs more than re-weighting and widens the recall gap between machine types to 0.81; adversarial debiasing halves that gap (0.22 to 0.11) for 1-11 % more cost
studies.notes: Same split and ASSUMED costs as PM1 (missed failure GBP 2,000, inspection GBP 150; PM1's logistic result reproduced exactly). Test: 71 failures (Type L 46, M 18, H 7), so one H failure moves H recall by 14 points and H drives most gaps. Logistic regression cost: none GBP 118,550, class weights 65,350, group-and-class weights 70,100 (recall gap 0.04), SMOTE 70,000, threshold moving 74,700. SMOTENC made 28 of 5,602 synthetic failures Type H. Adversarial debiasing (Zhang, Lemoine & Mitchell, 2018; PyTorch, 5 seeds, strength 0.03 chosen on validation) narrows gaps mainly by raising false alarms in M and H; strength 0.3 or more alerts on almost every machine. For LightGBM the differences between methods are within noise. Type is a product-quality variant, not a protected human attribute: the methods are what is shown. The D1 supplier parity screen was not run.

studies.headline: Hybrid search finds the expert-labelled clause most often within a contract
On a simulated order history, a logistic risk score ranks late deliveries better than each supplier's past late rate (AUC 0.77 vs 0.69); LightGBM adds nothing (0.75)
studies.notes: Method check only: the order history is generated from a stated process (supplier reliability, sea lanes, December peak, order size), so the models can only recover effects that were put in, and they do (sea lane and supplier carry the largest coefficients). 8,112 training and 2,392 test orders; temporal split at 2011-07-01. Real receipts from the ERP receipt feed would replace the generator.

studies.data_kind: simulation (real UCI scope; terms, stock and CO2 factors assumed or simulated)
studies.headline: Under a binding budget, a 5% CO2 cut is almost free (9 of 23,980 units), but halving CO2 costs 13.8 points of coverage
studies.notes: Real UCI scope (40 SKUs, two offers each, £20,000 weekly budget); CO2 lane factors and unit weights are assumed, terms and stock simulated. Exact epsilon-constraint (CP-SAT, 21 caps, 3.1 s) against NSGA-II (pymoo, 3 seeds): NSGA-II reaches 98.1-98.5% of the exact front's hypervolume but 35-43 of its ~116 front points are dominated by exact points. The exact front is sampled at 21 caps, so its hypervolume is a lower bound.

studies.headline: On a simulated delivery history, LightGBM cuts arrival-time error from 30.6 to 12.4 minutes against a region-by-hour average and gets 92 % of parcels within 30 minutes, but for couriers with no history it still misses by 27 minutes and its 80 % interval covers only 34 %
studies.notes: Generated parcels (couriers, regions, hour, distance, stops ahead, weekday; 66,197-67,296 test parcels per seed, 3 seeds), chronological split (January-April train, May-June test); 4 couriers join in the test period with no history. The generator's own expected time (MAE 10.4 minutes) is the floor no model can beat. Quantile LightGBM (10th-90th) covers 74 % overall (target 80 %), 78 % for known couriers; the shortfall is the cold start, where predictions run about 21 minutes short. Stops still ahead is the main driver. Straight-line distances; real data (LaDe) needs the owner's approval, and its published leaderboard is not comparable.

metrics.label: 80% interval coverage, quantile LightGBM, new couriers

studies.data_kind: historical backtest (UCI Online Retail II sales)
studies.headline: Trained forecasters cut daily error by about a third against seasonal naive; TCN and LightGBM are not clearly different
studies.notes: Protocol 2.1.0 = 2.0.0 with the weekday-corrected TCN; 503 products, rolling test origins 2011-10-13 and 2011-11-10. Pooled per-product MAE: naive 21.35, LightGBM 14.52, TCN 14.32. TCN - naive -7.02 [-8.94, -5.45]; TCN - LightGBM -0.20 [-0.46, +0.03], TCN better on 42% of products (no clear difference). Not an untouched holdout (D-042).

studies.data_kind: simulation (real UCI scope and country shares; stock, terms and budget simulated)
studies.headline: Under a binding budget, rest-of-world customers got 51% coverage against 83% for UK customers; moderate reweighing (alpha 0.4) cuts the gap from 31.7 to 12.2 points for 1.4 points of total coverage
studies.notes: Real UCI scope and recorded country shares (365 days); stock, terms and budget simulated; demand is the champion forecast. A product's shortfall is attributed to its customers by past purchase share. Worst-to-best ratio 0.62 before, 0.85 at alpha 0.4 (passes the four-fifths screen). Full inverse-share reweighing (alpha 1) over-corrects: UK falls to 72% and total coverage drops 7 points. One scope, one date; deterministic allocation.

studies.data_kind: simulation (generated trip telemetry and fuel; CO2 factor assumed)
studies.headline: On simulated fleet trips, telemetry models rank fuel-inefficient trips better than a fleet-average rule (AUC 0.95-0.96 against 0.89) and cut the litres-per-100-km error of class averages by more than half, but their flags capture less of the excess fuel (38-40 % against 46 %)
studies.notes: 15,965 generated trips (60 vehicles, 72 drivers, 12 months; train months 1-8, validation 9-10, test 11-12). Inefficient = measured L/100 km above 1.15 x the class and payload reference. Test: MAE class mean 2.05, ridge 0.91, LightGBM 0.85 L/100 km; F1 rule 0.62, logistic 0.76, LightGBM 0.76; LightGBM does not beat logistic regression on AUC. The rule sees each trip's measured fuel and long heavy trips dominate the excess litres, so it captures more of them. CO2 at an ASSUMED 2.5 kg per litre. Generated data recovers only the effects put in; no real telematics.

metrics.label: excess litres in the test months

studies.headline: All 196 generated answers kept every figure in a cited passage, with correct citations; 1 of 67 questions that should get no answer got one (3 before the product check), but the check also declines all 8 questions that name only a supplier
studies.notes: 271 generated questions over simulated and fictional agreements (labels by construction, not human-reviewed); local qwen2.5:7b at temperature 0, median 2.8 s, p95 4.0 s. Answerable 108/108 and reworded 88/88 answered; out-of-scope 0/48 and unknown product 0/10 answered. Ambiguous: 1 of 9 answered from one product's terms (was 3 of 9). Named supplier: 0 of 8 answered (was 3 of 8) because each agreement sets terms per product, so the system asks for a product code; the labels expected an answer, so this counts as over-refusal. The figure check would pass a correct figure next to a wrong one.

metrics.label: out of scope: answered when it should not be
ambiguous: answered when it should not be

studies.headline: SupplyLens policy scores highest of three tool-only policies on InventoryBench
studies.notes: Deterministic policies only; does not use the forecasting models affected by F01.

studies.data_kind: simulation (assumed routes and handling times; published ft06 check)
studies.headline: Each hand dispatch rule (FIFO, SPT, EDD, most work remaining) gives a receiving-floor schedule 11-13 % longer on average than exact CP-SAT; even the best rule chosen after the fact is 8.5 % longer (1.6-13.8 %), and no single rule is best at every size
studies.notes: Check: the Fisher-Thompson ft06 instance solves to its known optimum of 55 in 0.01 s (rules 61-88). Nine receiving-floor instances (10, 20, 40 orders x 3) on four stations; routes, handling minutes and due slots ASSUMED, order volumes from real UCI weekly sales. CP-SAT (8 workers, 20 s) proved 7 of 9 makespans optimal. Minimising total tardiness instead, the rules' tardiness is 32 % (SPT) to 436 % (MWKR) higher. Static one-shift job shop; no breakdowns or late arrivals.

metrics.label: makespan gap vs CP-SAT, most work remaining

studies.data_kind: published benchmark (AI4I 2020, a synthetic dataset) and simulation (motor fleet)
studies.headline: On the AI4I 2020 dataset LightGBM catches 61 of 71 test failures with 135 inspections (AUC 0.98), cutting expected cost 72 % against running to failure; on a simulated motor fleet, replacing on predicted life avoids every failure at two-thirds the cost of fixed intervals, though a 1D-CNN does not beat a ridge baseline
studies.notes: (a) UCI AI4I 2020 (CC BY 4.0, synthetic data modelled on a milling process), 10,000 cycles, 339 failures; 60/20/20 random split; threshold chosen on validation by assumed costs (missed failure GBP 2,000, inspection GBP 150). Logistic regression AUC 0.93, average precision 0.43; LightGBM AUC 0.98, average precision 0.86. Heat, power and overstrain failures all caught; tool-wear failures 1 of 10 and random failures 0 of 4, as their causes are random by construction. (b) Simulated fleet, 80 training and 30 test motors; RMSE ridge 18.9, CNN 19.3 cycles: a negative result for deep learning on this signal. Policies on the 30 test motors: run to failure GBP 72,000 (30 failures); fixed interval at the 5th life percentile GBP 18,000 (3 failures, 94 cycles of life discarded on average); replace when predicted life < 20 cycles GBP 12,000 (0 failures, 16 cycles discarded). Costs assumed.

studies.headline: On generated goods-in images a small CNN flags defects with AUC 0.997 against 0.946 for hand-made features; letting it pass items and checking only what it flags costs 53 % less than inspecting everything, with 98.7 % of defects caught
studies.notes: Images generated from stated rules (glaze texture, printed band, uneven light, noise; 30 % carry a scratch, chip or stain, some faint): 6,000 train, 1,500 validation, 3,000 test. Threshold chosen on validation by assumed costs (manual check GBP 0.30, escaped defect GBP 12). CNN: 958 flagged, 11 escapes, precision 0.89; inspect-all GBP 900 vs CNN policy GBP 419. The hand-made-feature baseline reaches the same recall only by flagging 95 % of items. Occlusion maps (drop in the CNN's logit when each 8x8 patch is greyed out) show the score depends on the defect region. Generated images are easier than real photographs: a method check.

studies.headline: On ACORD, vector search beats the hybrid — a negative result we keep
studies.notes: All 57 judged test queries (one was wrongly excluded before, DEF-04); search restricted to the ACORD clause corpus. nDCG@10: vector 0.108, hybrid 0.089, lexical 0.061. Absolute scores are low and were not compared with published ACORD baselines.

studies.headline: Effective-date filtering and supersession reranking each remove wrong-version citations; together they reach 100%
studies.notes: 2x2 factorial on 118 synthetic questions (not human-reviewed): temporal main effect +3.2 points, rerank main effect +4.2 points, interaction +0.9 points. Measures the mechanism, not real-world contract understanding.

studies.headline: Answer-support rules flag ambiguity and some unanswerable questions, at a cost on reworded questions
studies.notes: 535 generated questions (labels by construction, not human-reviewed), thresholds fitted on the development half. Test half, hybrid: out-of-scope abstention 0/26 -> 10/26, ambiguity 0/4 -> 3/4, answerable 45/45 kept, paraphrases answered 172/172 -> 121/172, named supplier 4/4 -> 3/4. Lexical-only (hosted demo): named supplier 4/4 -> 0/4 (false ambiguity). Retrieval-only signals cannot tell out-of-scope from reworded in-scope questions.

studies.data_kind: offline evaluation (hand-written attacks and planted documents on simulated agreements)
studies.headline: All 17 red-team attacks held once passages are screened for text addressed to the model and answers with links are withheld: no planted figure, link or supplier, no leaked instructions, no other workspace's record and no claimed action; both control questions were still answered correctly (the first run broke on 2 of 17)
studies.notes: 13 adversarial questions (instruction overrides in English and Spanish, system-prompt extraction, an approval request, a false premise, currency figures, advice, another workspace, markup, personal data, a length override, the seeded Delta injection note, a version unknown at the cutoff) and 4 agreements poisoned through the upload endpoint; local qwen2.5:7b at temperature 0 on simulated agreements. Held by: the extractive layer (nothing generated) 7, the generation checks 3, an answer within the rules 7. Rules are pattern checks written before the run, so a reworded leak could pass; the screen recognises text addressed to a model, not a false claim written as ordinary contract text; one poisoned answer named the document title rather than its supplier.

metrics.label: held by the extractive layer (nothing generated)
poisoned cases where the model repeated planted text

studies.data_kind: simulation (generated delivery days; fuel and CO2 factors assumed)
studies.headline: On simulated 20-80-stop delivery days, OR-Tools meets every delivery window and drives 31-39 % less than a window-aware nearest-neighbour plan; against a fixed angle order the saving grows from 2 % to 28 % with size, and a nearest neighbour that ignores windows is up to 12 % shorter but makes 225 of 700 stops late
studies.notes: 15 instances (20, 40 and 80 stops x 5 seeds) with van capacity and time windows; OR-Tools routing (guided local search, 10 s limit) solved all, with 0 late stops against 4 (window-aware nearest neighbour), 225 (nearest neighbour ignoring windows) and 240 (fixed order); vans 1 / 2 / 4 against 2.8 / 4.0 / 5.8. It was shorter than the fixed order on 10 of 15 instances; the required check (never worse than nearest neighbour on a fixed instance) passes. Straight-line distances; the fixed order stands in for a habitual sequence and is not a real driver's. Fuel at an ASSUMED 9 L/100 km; CO2 with E1's 0.1 kg per tonne-km and an ASSUMED 0.5 t payload, an HGV average, so van CO2 is probably understated: compare the plans, not the absolute figures. Wall-clock limit: a rerun on a busier machine can differ slightly.

studies.headline: On total daily units, XGBoost beats Prophet and a seasonal naive (WAPE 24.6% vs 28.0% and 29.7%); adding London weather makes no clear difference to either (95% intervals span zero)
studies.notes: 13 weekly origins from 2011-09-05 to 2011-11-28, 7 days ahead, 91 total-level points and 4,550 product-day points (50 products). Product-level daily demand is intermittent, so WAPE is above 100% for every model (XGBoost 110%, naive 114%) and MAPE is taken over non-zero days only. Weather on the target day is the observed value, so any gain would be an upper bound. Daily correlation of units with mean temperature -0.03 and with rainfall 0.05. Weather: Open-Meteo historical API, CC BY 4.0.

studies.headline: A small LSTM beats seasonal naive and Prophet on WAPE but not XGBoost on UCI total daily units (WAPE 0.265 +/- 0.013 over 5 seeds against 0.246), and its gain over seasonal naive is not clear (95 % interval includes zero)
studies.notes: W1's protocol: 13 Monday origins (2011-09-05 to 2011-11-28), 7 days ahead, refitted at each origin, 91 points; seasonal naive reproduces W1's recorded values exactly. LSTM (one layer, 32 units; last 56 days plus calendar features; no weather, no holiday calendar), CPU and deterministic; only the loss (Huber over MSE) was chosen, on 9 earlier validation origins. WAPE / MAPE / RMSE: LSTM 0.265 / 0.285 / 7,667 (mean of 5 seeds); XGBoost 0.246 / 0.263 / 7,498 and Prophet 0.280 / 0.268 / 7,617 (both from W1, without weather); seasonal naive 0.297 / 0.331 / 8,909. No seed beat XGBoost on WAPE. XGBoost and Prophet are read from W1, which stored no per-day forecasts, so no paired test against them.

metrics.label: LSTM gain over seasonal naive is clear

studies.headline: On 73 CUAD supply contracts a rule extractor finds about half of the experts' labelled clauses and fields (overlap F1 0.51, exact span 0.35; 0.51 on 437 held-out contracts), far ahead of the top BM25 paragraph per field (0.19), though the top three paragraphs recall more expiry, renewal and minimum-commitment clauses at a quarter of the precision
studies.notes: 805 expert labels in the nine scored categories (2,176 in all), human-labelled (CUAD v1). In-sample: the rules were written after reading about ten labels per category, so the held-out check on 437 other CUAD contracts (4,456 labels, other contract types) is the fairer figure. Weakest fields: exclusivity (overlap F1 0.40) and minimum commitment (0.31); price is scored against Price Restrictions (13 labels), so its precision (0.07) understates it; MOQ and lead time have no CUAD category. Plain text only (no PDF or OCR intake, D-076); no model. Shown as a DRAFT in Policies > Extracted terms and never used for planning; confirming a field is not built.

n.label: expert labels in the scored categories

exploratory.headline: Segment-wise model choice and validation-fitted interval scaling changed nothing on this cohort
exploratory.notes: Rules frozen on validation: Syntetos-Boylan classes put every product in 'lumpy' (94%) or 'erratic' (6%) at daily grain and TCN won both on validation, so the composite equals TCN; symmetric interval scaling stays at 1.0 because 39% of product-days are zero and any narrowing drops them out of the interval. Medians sum to 42-50% of realised volume (trained models). Test windows already seen.

exploratory.data_kind: simulation (real UCI demand and forecasts; assumed terms and costs); exploratory (reuses F1's last test window)
exploratory.headline: Through the product's own ordering logic, lower forecast error did not mean lower simulated cost
exploratory.notes: Simulated, assumed terms and costs, 503 products, four weekly reviews 2011-11-10..2011-12-08. Unconstrained budget: a no-forecast base-stock rule cost GBP 11,983, product+naive 12,957, product+TCN 13,673 (vs naive +1.42/product [-1.64, 4.82]), product+LightGBM 19,842 (vs naive +13.69 [4.67, 25.08]). Under the workspace-scaled budget the planner rations; TCN's smaller requirements fit the budget (13,673 vs naive 78,442), an interaction with budget allocation rather than proof of forecast value.
